neighbours.label: the blacksmith's forge: blacksmiths and farriers, the forge, the anvil and hammering hot iron; other metal trades (welding, locksmithing, goldsmithing) and the surname Smith stay low
fire: The blacksmith pumped the bellows until the coals glowed.
Medieval villages relied on the smith to mend ploughs.
He laid the red-hot iron on the anvil and struck it.
Sparks scattered across the floor of the forge.
The museum keeps a working forge where visitors can watch iron being shaped.
A blacksmith's apprentice learned to make nails first.
The heavy anvil had sat in the same smithy for a century.
She took up blacksmithing and now forges garden gates.
quiet: The baker fed the oven until the bricks glowed.
Medieval villages relied on the miller to grind grain.
He laid the wet clay on the wheel and shaped it.
Sparks scattered across the floor of the welding shop.
The museum keeps a working loom where visitors can watch cloth being woven.
A locksmith's apprentice learned to cut keys first.
The heavy piano had sat in the same parlour for a century.
She took up knitting and now makes garden-party shawls.
neighbours.short: the blacksmith's forge (smiths, anvils, hot iron)
